entries.title: Isaiah 30:1
segments:
In this and the following chapter, the prophet rebukes the Jews for resorting to Egypt, rather than to the living God, for help against the Assyrians.  The occasion was the invasion of Sennacherib; but here, as in the preceding chapter, he looks far beyond that event to the final issue of God's dealings with his covenant people. 
 
  Cover with a covering; protect themselves against their foes.  Some render, "make a league." 
 
vv 1-7. 
 
"An evil heart of unbelief in departing from the living God." is the great sin of the human race.  This has in all ages led nations and families, as well as individuals, to seek help in trouble from man rather than from God, and always to their disappointment and ruin.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:4
segments:
His princes--ambassadors; Judah's princes and ambassodors. 
 
  Zoan; in lower Egypt. 
 
  Hanes; in middle Egypt.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:5
segments: They were all ashamed; Judah's ambassadors.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:6
segments:
The burden of the beasts of the south; "the beasts of the south" are the beasts which carry the treasures of Judah into the south, that is, into Egypt, for the purpose of securing the alliance and help of the Egyptians.  In the word "burden" there is a double allusion, first to the load of treasures, secondly to the threatened wrath of God upon the undertaking. 
 
  The land of trouble--fiery flying serpent; a description of the southern desert, through which the road to Egypt lies.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:7
segments: Their strength is to sit still; their boasted help ends in their doing nothing.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:8
segments:
vv 8-14. 
 
Wicked men desire to hear not what is true, but what will flatter them in their sins.  Thus they reject the only way of salvation, and bring upon themselves irremedible ruin.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:11
segments: Cause the Holy One of Israel to cease; let us hear no more concerning him.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:13
segments:
This iniquity; the iniquity described in the preceding verses, the root of which is an unbelieving spirit. 
 
  Shall be to you as a breach--in a high wall; this sin shall make Judah like a falling wall, which swells out gradually more and more, and at last falls suddenly.  The "breach" here is the broken part of the wall.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:14
segments:
He shall break it; God shall break the wall, which represents the Jewish state. 
 
  A sherd; a broken piece of the vessel. 
 
  To take fire--to take water; large enough for these purposes.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:15
segments:
Returning and rest; returning to God and resting in his promises. 
 
They who, in times of trouble and danger, honor God with the full confidence of their souls, shall receive from him inward peace and comfort, and also outward deliverance, so far as their highest welfare requires it.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:16
segments:
We will flee; will escape from the enemy. 
 
  Shall ye flee; fly before the enemy. 
 
When men refuse to give God their confidence, he makes their devices for obtaining deliverance the means of their destruction.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:17
segments: A beacon--ensign; standing solitary and desolate.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:18
segments: Therefore; because in God is salvation,
, and in man's help is only disappointment and ruin,

. 
 
  Wait, that he may be gracious--be exalted, that he may have mercy; God's long-suffering, and the manifestation of his greatness, both have for their end to bring men, through repentance, to the enjoyment of his forgiving love. 
 
  Judgment; righteousness and faithfulness.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:19
segments: The people; the pious remnant.  The prophet, after his usual manner, turns from threatenings to promises.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:20
segments: The most prosperous days of God's people have often been those of great temporal suffering.  It is far better to have spiritual life and health with outward affliction, than worldly prosperity with spiritual darkness and deadness.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:21
segments:
A word behind thee; the voice of God following them in their wanderings from duty. 
 
They who faithfully attend to the monitions of God's word and providence, will not fall into dangerous error.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:22
segments:
Covering--ornament; the overlaying of silver or gold, which is mentioned as the most valuable part of the idol.  They defile them by casting them away with abhorrence as unclean things. 
 
vv 22-23. 
 
Repentance, and fruits worthy of repentance, bring a return of God's favor.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:24
segments:
Ear; plough. 
 
  Clean; or, "savory."  The abundance and good quality of the provender are an emblem of the universal plenty that prevails.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:25
segments:
Rivers and streams; filling them with verdure and fruitfulness. 
 
  In the day of the great slaughter; here, as elsewhere, this golden age of the church is represented as introduced by the slaughter of God's foes. 
 
  Towers; of the enemy.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:26
segments: As the light of the sun--sevenfold; this is the era of millennial glory, perhaps also with a reference to the perfect blessedness of heaven.  Compare

. 
 
The universal prevalence of the gospel among men will fill the world with such light and gladness as we are unable to conceive of, and all this will be but a foretaste of the eternal blessedness of heaven.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:27
segments:
vv 27-32. 
 
The same divine judgments which destroy the wicked, bring gladness and salvation to the righteous.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:28
segments:
His breath; his anger, which is compared to an overflowing stream. 
 
  Reach to the midst of the neck; a proverbial expression for imminent danger.

The sieve of vanity; the sieve of perdition. 
 
  A bridle--causing them to err; the bridle is the delusions which lead them astray, here represented as a judgment proceeding from God. Compare

entries.title: Isaiah 30:29
segments:
Ye shall have a song; God's people, when he thus destroys their foes. 
 
  Into the mountain of the Lord; to celebrate there the yearly festivals.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:31
segments: The Assyrian; Sennacherib.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:32
segments:
The grounded staff; the ordained rod. 
 
  Shall pass; upon the Assyrian. 
 
  With taberets and harps; on the part of God's people. 
 
  Battles of shaking; tumultuous battles. 
 
  He fight with it; God, against Assyria.

entries.title: Isaiah 30:33
segments: Topet; the funeral pile for God's enemies, in allusion to Topet, where the idolatrous Jews offered their children as burnt-sacrifices to Moloch.
For the king; for Jehovah.  Under this terrible image is represented the final vengeance of God upon his foes, of which their temporal destruction is but the beginning. Compare

. 
 
The terrible effects of God's wrath in this world are a solemn foreshadowing of its power in that prison of despair "where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched."
